preamble: Owner rulings that shape the kit. The evidence for each lives in docs/design.md §5.

decisions.text: Name: houserules (was lorekit). docs/design.md §5.1.
License: MIT, with SPDX headers in the kit-owned scripts. docs/design.md §5.2.
Publishing: deferred. No remote, no npm publish, no marketplace registration until the owner rules. docs/design.md §5.3.
tag-pilot adoption: deferred until PR #42 is merged; tag-pilot stays the upstream of the kit-owned files until then. docs/design.md §5.4.
Dogfooding: this repository installs its own kit (id prefix HR); the root copies stay equal to template/. docs/design.md §5.5.
SessionStart matcher: startup|resume|clear|fork for the ritual, compact for the standing rules. docs/design.md §5.6.

Bootstrap exception: batch 1 (spec 'batch 0') was implemented by the orchestrator on Fable without a mightier reviewer, because the agent layer was installed only by its last task. From batch 2 on, every change goes through implementer, task-reviewer, and branch-reviewer under process.model-policy.
Package manager: pnpm only, never npm or npx; the workspace follows tag-pilot (exact mise pins for node and pnpm, pnpm-lock.yaml, mise tasks setup, test, lint, audit). docs/design.md §5.7.

Commit body line limit in the audit: process.conventional-commits sets body_line_max 100 in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json once HR-006 ships the check. docs/design.md §5.8.

process.rulings-to-file body gains the dispatch-deviation bullet: a deviation from the spec's process line (model, order, gate) is a ruling to amend in the same turn (the home-file and ledger bullets were already present); applied in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json. docs/design.md §5.9.

process.tdd summary names the disclosed-mutation proof for already-correct behavior (shortened to the 160-character cap; the body keeps the detail); applied in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json. docs/design.md §5.10.

quality.principles body gains the test-state-hygiene bullet (behavior-asserting tests that can fail; explicit afterEach reset for module-mock factories); applied in knowledge/quality.json and template/knowledge/quality.json. docs/design.md §5.11.

process.rulings-to-file summary includes a deferral’s backlog item (one word shorter than quoted at the gate, for the 160-character cap); applied in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json. docs/design.md §5.12.

tag-pilot adoption: deferred again (the PR #42 trigger fired); new trigger: the first houserules release or publish, raised together with decision 3. Until then tag-pilot stays the upstream of the kit-owned files. docs/design.md §5.4.

process.tdd body gains the fix-round and reconstruction clauses (a narrowing/widening fix round carries its own RED or counter-example; a post-commit cycle says so and keeps the real order); applied in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json. docs/design.md §5.13.

process.rulings-to-file body gains the accepted-deviation clause (home it in the turn it is accepted, before the next dispatch); applied in knowledge/process.json and template/knowledge/process.json. docs/design.md §5.14.

Releases: semver via release-please, changelogs generated from the conventional commits; the first release is a pre-release under the alpha dist-tag; the GitHub upstream is created right after the alpha-state tasks are done — until then decision 3's no-remote constraint stands. docs/design.md §5.19.

Upstream go (alpha state reached at batch 11): a public GitHub repository named houserules under the owner's account; main pushed; release-please activates on the push. The npm publish under the alpha dist-tag stays pending decision 3's publish part. docs/design.md §5.19.

Release tag format (Tier-2 spec ruling 1): plain v<version> — include-component-in-tag goes false in the release-please config at the next config-touching task; an alias tag v0.2.0-alpha points at the existing release commit so the grammar is uniform from the first release; houserules-v0.2.0-alpha stays as history. Unblocks HR-048's channels and HR-049. docs/design.md §5.20.

Implementation language (Tier-2 spec ruling 2): Rust — type-level correctness with serde modeling the schemas exactly, smaller binaries, no GC; cross-compilation and the release matrix (cargo-dist or cross/zig) are spec decisions. Chosen over Go with the trade-offs on the table. docs/design.md §5.21.

npm retires (Tier-2 spec ruling 3): distribution is binary-only (ubi, asdf, taps, curl installer); package.json remains for this repository's own dev tooling; the README's post-publish npm form goes away at the rewrite; an esbuild-style wrapper package stays purely additive later if demand appears. This closes decision 3's npm part — no npm publish, ever, under the current ruling. docs/design.md §5.22.

Tier-2 surface and runtime (spec-gate rulings 4-7): no shims — tools/kb.sh and tools/backlog.sh are deleted and update gains KIT_OWNED deletion; flat commands with per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) plus a built-in check-commit replacing the hook's commitlint probe; houserules becomes modular (adopters choose feature sets — HR-053, after the port); the dev tooling migrates too — cargo test replaces vitest phase by phase, and pnpm, package.json, and node_modules leave the tree at retirement. Nothing JS survives phase 5. docs/design.md §5.23.

Post-port repository sweep (Tier-2 spec ruling 8): the migration closes with a full-repository scan that corrects every rule, knowledge entry, backlog item, and doc (README included) to the new setup; standing entries that encode the old world amend or retire under recorded rulings; historical records keep their wording; mechanical grep gate as phase 5's closing task. docs/design.md §5.24.

Glob vocabulary for the Rust port (mid batch 16): globset becomes the single matching engine; every divergence from the frozen JS union is pinned by a counterexample test asserting the chosen answer; malformed globs are named errors, never panics; extglob leaves the vocabulary. The one further sanctioned parity exception beside the flat surface. docs/design.md §5.25.

The five batch-16 parity deviations confirmed as a set at the batch report: named-line exit-2 failure paths; eager glob validation; engine-decided regex verdicts with only V8 reason wording diverging; per-ported-file coverage ratchets with global floors intact; named findings where the JS crashed. docs/design.md §5.26; spec §6 carries the detail.

Rust toolchain pin form: stable, freshest — bumps track stable's newest immediately, the quarantine bypass deliberate; the version is CLI-resolved and pinned exactly (moved to 1.98.1 at the ruling). Procedure houserules.rust-toolchain-bumps-use-stable. docs/design.md §5.27.

Batch 16 retrospective standing changes, all four approved: the code-comment-is-not-a-home-file bullet on process.rulings-to-file; the language-engine bullet on quality.principles; new standing rules process.evidence-outlives-the-session and process.claims-match-artifacts. Applied in knowledge/ and template/knowledge/. docs/design.md §5.28.

The three batch-17 rulings confirmed as a set at the batch report: the data-layer rule (typed models only for never-re-serialized, parse-failure-tolerant paths; consumerless models delete), the unified get’s arity-first ordering, and the clap argv deviation with every observable instance pinned by scripted enumeration. docs/design.md §5.29; spec §3 and §6 carry the detail.

Batch 17 standing approvals, all five, with the Rust-tooling correction: the report-claims checker mandate (HR-061 ports it to a cargo bin - no Node tools in the codebase), the code-comments measurement clause, the exact-pins Cargo extension, the scratch-dirs sanctioned-forms bullet, and the new standing rules closure-claims-carry-enumeration and review-findings-are-claims-too. make-corpus.mjs stays the one interim exception (drives the frozen JS; retires with the corpus), pending confirmation. docs/design.md §5.30.
